main_body: Tall palm-like tree: a long brown trunk (about 36 rows) topped by a spreading dark-green frond canopy with a light-green crown on top
top_band: light green crown rows 2-6 (L~142) at x=16, then a dark step at row 7 (L=19) into the dark frond mass below
evidence: The column at x=16 reads as a lighter horizontal crown surface of 5 rows, an abrupt drop to dark fronds, and then a vertical trunk below. The fronds spread out and shade the trunk, so the canopy reads as a surface seen from above and the trunk as the south face. This is an organic plant, not a flat elevation. The marks are weak: there is no distinct edge line, and the crown is only a small patch of the canopy. It passes narrowly.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours for the references. The canopy has about 4 green steps with no leaf clumps or per-leaf highlights, so it reads as a few mid-dark blocks. The trunk is a plain two-tone stripe repeated every 2 rows, which is mechanical and has no bark grain, roots or flare. Outlines are tinted dark green or brown rather than neutral, and there are no flat fills of 5x5 or larger. Even so, the piece is far thinner and simpler than the lush, richly shaded Beodeul trees.
